# Helping your midwife find you

## A warm welcome from Riverside community midwives

Planning a home birth? We’re looking forward to coming to you. In the Philippines, there’s a saying that a midwife is like family. That’s how we hope you’ll feel about us: we’re coming to care for you, and we want you to feel at home with us.

First, though, we need to find your home! A little planning now can save time when labour starts. It also means you won’t have to explain which of the five identical gates is yours at 3am.

## First things first: when to call

Our home birth cover starts from **37 weeks of pregnancy**.

- **If you think labour has started before 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line straight away.** You will need to go to hospital rather than plan for your baby to be born at home.
- **From 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line when labour starts.** The line will put you in touch with the midwife who is on call.
- Please **do not call your midwife’s personal mobile** when labour starts. They may not be working, and we don’t want your call to be missed.

Keep the birth line number somewhere easy to find, and save it in your phone. If you’re unsure whether labour has started, or you’re worried about yourself or your baby, call the birth line for advice. You don’t have to work it out on your own.

**Riverside birth line:** ______________________________________

## Make your home easy to spot

Your home may be easy to find in daylight, but streets can look very different in the dark or rain. A few little clues can make all the difference.

### Check your number or house name

Can your house number be seen clearly from the road? If your home has a name instead of a number, please make sure the name is easy to see too.

One of us once went looking for *Rosemary Cottage* on a street of terraced houses. The sat nav took her to a chippy. Lovely as a chippy is, it wasn’t where the baby was being born!

When you call, tell the midwife anything that might help, such as:

- The colour of your front door or gate.
- A nearby landmark.
- Whether your house name or number is hard to see.
- Which entrance to use.

### Leave a light on

If it’s dark, please switch on your porch or outside light if you have one. A light in a front window can help too.

One family tied balloons to their gate, like they were having a party. We found them straight away! You’re very welcome to do something similar if you like, but there’s no need to buy anything special.

### Help us find the right door

If you live in a block of flats, please tell us:

- The name or number of your building.
- Which entrance to use.
- Your floor and flat number.
- Any door-entry code, or how we should contact you to be let in.
- Whether there’s anything unusual about the layout.

Please don’t assume we’ll find flat 14 next to flat 13! One of us spent 20 minutes driving around a block in Everton before finding out that the flat was in a different building. In the end, Dad waved a tea towel from the window. It worked, but a few directions might be easier on everyone’s arms.

If there’s more than one door or building, tell us which one is yours. We want to come straight to you—not accidentally join someone else for a cup of tea. One of us once walked into the wrong open house and was offered a Jammie Dodger by a very nice gentleman!

## Send us a pin or location

If it helps, you can send a location pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone, or give the team your **what3words** location. Ask your midwife how to share this with the team.

A pin or what3words location is especially helpful if your home is hard to find, but please also give us your full address and any useful directions. Technology is handy, but it doesn’t always tell us which door to knock on.

## Make space for the midwives

Two midwives come for the birth, usually in separate cars. If possible, please leave **two parking spaces** nearby.

We bring quite a lot with us: gas and air cylinders, a big bag and sometimes birthing pool equipment. Our arms will thank you if we can park close to your home!

Some streets around **Anfield and Kensington** are in permit zones. If you live in one, please check with the council about visitor parking before your due date. Have any visitor permits ready as needed, including one on the dashboard if that’s how your permit works. Nobody wants a parking ticket as a souvenir of your baby’s birthday.

If parking near your home is difficult, don’t worry. Just let us know when you call so we can plan where to go.

## Give us a clear way in

Please keep the path to your door, hallway and stairs as clear as you can. Moving shoes, washing baskets and toys out of the way will help us get in safely while carrying equipment.

No judgement here: we know a family home is a lived-in home. But stepping on Lego while carrying a gas cylinder is an experience we’d all rather avoid.

Please also think about how we’ll get through the door. If someone is with you and able to let us in, that’s great. If you’re on your own or getting to the door might be difficult, tell the midwife when you call so you can make a plan together.

## A little help with pets

We love meeting your pets, but please put them in another room before the midwives arrive, if you can. That gives us space to bring in the equipment and care for you safely.

We once met a very friendly Staffie called Pippin, who loved one of us *so much* that she nearly dropped the gas and air. Pippin meant well, but we’d rather meet your pets properly after everything has settled down!

## Ready for the fridge?

You can tick these off as you get ready. Please don’t worry if you can’t do everything—just tell us anything we need to know when you call.

### Helping your midwife find you: checklist

☐ I have saved the **Riverside birth line** number and know where to find it.

☐ I know to **call the birth line when labour starts**, not my midwife’s personal mobile.

☐ I know that **home birth cover starts at 37 weeks**. If I think labour has started before then, I will call the birth line straight away and will need to go to hospital.

☐ My house number or name is easy to see, or I have another way to help the midwife spot my home.

☐ I have useful directions ready, including the right building, entrance and floor if I live in a flat.

☐ I know how I can share a location pin or what3words location if needed.

☐ I can switch on an outside light or a light in a front window when it’s dark.

☐ I have thought about where **two midwives can park**, and checked visitor permits if needed.

☐ The way to the front door, hallway and stairs can be kept clear.

☐ I have a plan for letting the midwives in.

☐ I have a plan to put any pets in another room.

**Birth line number:** _________________________________________

**Helpful directions or parking information:** ________________________

__________________________________________________________

We’re looking forward to meeting you and your baby. And if you do need to wave a tea towel, we’ll be looking out for you!
